chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Wallad, who said:

Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام said: “Regarding a man who is killed and has no heir except the Imam: indeed, it is not for the Imam to pardon; rather, he may kill [in retaliation] or take the blood-money and place it in the treasury of the Muslims, because the liability concerning the slain person was upon the Imam, and likewise his blood-money belongs to the Imam of the Muslims.”

key_terms.إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Imam who holds authority on behalf of the Muslim community
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood-money, the financial compensation due in a homicide case
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the legitimate Muslim authority who assumes guardianship when no private heir exists
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.جِنَايَةَ: the legal consequence or liability arising from the offense
key_terms.وَلِيٌّ: the legal heir or guardian entitled to pursue retaliation or accept compensation
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: is killed; refers to the victim of homicide

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a murdered person has no heir except the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a murdered person who has no wali other than the Imam. It states that the Imam may enforce qisas or accept diyah for the Muslim treasury, and that he does not have the option of pardoning in such a case because the right of guardianship returns to the Imam.
